Rashi on Yevamot 54b:10:1.english: One who performs the initial stage of intercourse with an animal - [Meaning] that he did not complete his intercourse.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:10:2.hebrew: ואחות אב ואחות אם - לאו מחייבי מיתות הן, דלא כתיבא בהו מיתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:10:2.english: And a father's sister and a mother's sister - They are not [among] those liable to death penalties, for death is not written regarding them.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:11:1.hebrew: ליכתבה במיתת בית דין - כגון באמו וחמותו, ולימא נמי: אם אינו ענין להו — דאתיא בהיקישא דר' יונה — תנהו ענין לבהמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:11:1.english: Let [Scripture] write it with regard to [a prohibition punishable by] capital punishment from the court - For example, with regard to his mother and his mother-in-law, and let [the Gemara] also say: If [that mention of he'erah] has no application to them — since it is [already] derived through the scriptural analogy (hekkesh) of Rabbi Yonah — apply it to [the case of] an animal.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:12:1.hebrew: איידי דכוליה קרא - דכתיב באחות אב ואחות אם בפרשת קדושים תהיו, לדרשא אתא כדתניא לקמן, כתיב ביה נמי העראה בלא צורך, לדרשא דבהמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:12:1.english: Since the entire verse - which is written regarding a father's sister and a mother's sister in the portion of Kedoshim Tihyu, comes for an exposition, as is taught in a baraita below, [the term indicating] the initial stage of intercourse is also written in it unnecessarily, for the exposition regarding bestiality.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:13:1.english: The nakedness of your father’s sister - [It] cites the earlier verse, from Acharei Mot.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:13:2.english: Whether - [Meaning] she is your father's sister from the father, [or] whether from the mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:14:1.english: Just as his sister, whether from the father or from the mother - For it is written: "the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother."

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:15:1.hebrew: מה דודתו מן האב ולא מן האם - שאם היה דודו אחי אביו מן האם ולא מן האב, אין אשתו עליו ערוה. ולקמן בעי מנלן:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:15:1.english: Just as his aunt [is] from the father and not from the mother - For if his uncle was his father's brother from the mother and not from the father, his wife is not a forbidden relative to him. And later [the Gemara] asks from where we [derive] this.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:16:1.english: His aunt — her prohibition does not come upon him on its own - rather, through his uncle's betrothal.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:17:1.hebrew: ולא תוכיח אחותו - וכיון דלא נפקא לן מדינא, תלמוד לומר מקרא שני בפרשת קדושים תהיו: "ערות אחות אביך ואחות אמך לא תגלה". ואין צריך להזהיר, שכבר הזהיר, ולא הוה ליה לאשמועינן אלא עונש, כדעבד באשת אח ובאחותו — "איש כי יקח אחות אביו ואחות אמו עונם ישאו" — וקרא יתירא הוא לרבות אחות אביו מן האם ואחות אמו מן האם:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:17:1.english: And his sister cannot prove [otherwise] - Since we cannot derive [this] from logical inference, Scripture states a second verse in the portion of Kedoshim Tihyu: "The nakedness of your father's sister and your mother's sister you shall not uncover." Now, it did not need to issue a warning, since it had already issued a warning [earlier], and it only needed to teach us [the] punishment — just as it did with a brother's wife and with his sister — "A man who takes his father's sister and his mother's sister, they shall bear their sin." Thus, it is a superfluous verse, [written] to include his father's sister from [the same] mother and his mother's sister from [the same] mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:19:1.hebrew: למה לי למכתב - האי קרא יתירא בתרוייהו, לכתוב בחדא ותיתי אידך מינה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:19:1.english: Why do I [need the Torah] to write - This verse is superfluous with regard to both of them; let [the Torah] write [it] regarding one, and let the other be derived from it.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:19:2.hebrew: יש לה חייס - דמשפחת אב קרויה משפחה, דכתיב: "ויתילדו על משפחותם לבית אבותם" (במדבר א׳:י״ח):
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:19:2.english: She has lineage - For a father's family is called "family," as it is written: "and they traced their lineage by their families, according to their fathers' houses" (Numbers 1:18).

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:1:1.hebrew: ביומי תליא מילתא - אפי' אם מת האוסרה, שפסקה דם בראייה ראשונה, אסורה כל שבעה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:1:1.english: The matter depends upon days - Even if that which renders her forbidden has died, [meaning] that she ceased [discharging] blood after the first sighting, she is forbidden all seven [days].

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:1:2.hebrew: בבנים תליא - אם יש לה בנים, אפילו מת אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:1:2.english: [It] depends upon children - If she has children, [she remains forbidden] even if his brother died.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:2:1.hebrew: אין אוסרן מתירן - אין כח באוסר להתיר, אלא דבר אחר מתירה. ימים מתירין את הנדה, ואשת אח כשהוא ערירי:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:2:1.english: What renders them prohibited does not render them permitted - That which renders [her] prohibited has no power to permit [her]; rather, something else permits her. Days permit the menstruating woman, and [for] a brother's wife, [it is] when he [dies] childless.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:3:1.hebrew: הוקשו כל העריות לנדה - שהרי כאן הוקשו כולן זו לזו, ונדה כתובה בפרשת עריות. הלכך, בהעראה ילפינן כולהו מנדה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:3:1.english: All forbidden relations are compared to a menstruating woman - For here they are all compared to one another, and a menstruating woman is written in the passage of forbidden relations. Therefore, regarding the initial stage of intercourse, we derive all of them from a menstruating woman.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:4:1.english: Niddah that is written with regard to a brother’s wife - From which we derived above ha’ara’ah [the initial stage of intercourse] for a brother’s wife from niddah.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:4:2.english: In her husband’s lifetime - If his brother divorced her.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:6:1.english: And a prohibition that stems from a positive commandment [has the status of] a positive commandment - But there is no karet.

Rashi on Yevamot 54b:9:1.hebrew: משכבי אשה - וכיון דבאשה הוי העראה משכב, ממילא איתסרא בזכור, דהא בזכור כתיב משכבי אשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 54b:9:1.english: The lyings of a woman - And since with a woman the initial stage of intercourse is [considered] lying, it is automatically forbidden with a male, for regarding a male it is written, "the lyings of a woman."

Tosafot on Yevamot 54b:4:1.hebrew: אלא רמז ליבמה שאסורה בחיי בעלה מנין - דכיון דשריא רחמנא אחר מיתה, אין סברא לומר דאסירא בחיי בעלה, דלא מיסתבר שהיה בא הכתוב לומר דאתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, אי לאו דמוכח קרא בהדיא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54b:4:1.english: Rather, from where is there a hint that a yevama is forbidden in her husband’s lifetime? - For since the Merciful One permitted her after [her husband’s] death, there is no logical reason to say that she is forbidden in her husband’s lifetime, as it is not reasonable that Scripture would come to say that a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative commandment that carries karet, were it not that the verse proves it explicitly.

Tosafot on Yevamot 54b:9:1.hebrew: בזכור מהו - הא דלא יליף זכור ובהמה מהקישא דרבי יונה, משום ד"את מקורה הערה" כתיב, והנהו לא שייך בהו מקור; ועוד, דאפסקינהו בקרא דמולך. אי נמי, משום דזכור ובהמה לא חשיב ביאה, דאין דרך ביאה בכך; ולהכי בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין נד:) צריך אזהרה ועונש לשוכב ונשכב בזכור, אע"ג דבעלמא לא בעי קרא לחייב האשה הנשכבת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 54b:9:1.english: With regard to a male, what is [the halakha]? - The reason [the Gemara] does not derive [the initial stage of intercourse with] a male and an animal from Rabbi Yonah's analogy [hekesh] [is] because it is written, "he has uncovered her source [mekorah]" [Leviticus 20:18], and [the term] "source" does not apply to those; and furthermore, because [Scripture] interrupted [the sequence of forbidden relations] with the verse of Molech. Alternatively, [it is] because [intercourse with] a male or an animal is not considered [a standard act of] intercourse, as that is not the normal manner of intercourse; and therefore, in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 54b), a prohibition and a punishment are needed for both the active partner and the passive partner in [homosexual intercourse with] a male, even though elsewhere [in the Torah] a verse is not needed to obligate the woman who is lain with.
